Chapter 8. The Darkness and the Cry: When God Feels Far Away.
There are times in life when everything just seems to go dark. You know those moments—when hope feels miles away, and it’s almost like God is silent. Picture the scene: Jesus, hanging on the cross, the sky turning dark overhead, and suddenly, his voice breaks through the gloom—“My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
That wasn’t just a moment in history. It was a cry that’s echoed in the heart of anyone who’s ever felt alone or abandoned. Maybe you’ve been there—sitting quietly, wrestling with questions that don’t have easy answers. The darkness on that day wasn’t only about the sky; it was emotional, spiritual. It was the feeling that even God had turned away.
The truth is, most of us have felt that way at some point. Wondering if our prayers are even being heard. Wondering if our pain really matters.
But here’s something powerful: that cry from the cross is a reminder that even in our deepest darkness, every feeling is understood. Jesus didn’t bottle up his pain or pretend to have it all together. He let out the ache, the confusion, the longing to feel close again.
What does that mean for us? It shows that faith isn’t about never doubting or never hurting. It’s about bringing every emotion—every fear, every question—into the open.
So if you’re feeling abandoned or alone, hear this: you’re not alone in your pain. The cross is where every cry is heard, where every darkness is shared.
The invitation? Bring every feeling, every question, every doubt. Even if the answer doesn’t come right away—even in the silence—love is still there, holding you steady.
